name: Horn of Echeyakee
summary: At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn gives hunters the Horn of Echeyakee to sound among the ancient kodo remains northeast of the settlement. Its call brings forth the legendary white predator of the Barrens.

sections.title: Calling the Whitemist
sections.body: Hunters receive the horn when they are tested in the hunt. Its call summons Echeyakee, whose name means “Whitemist” in Taur-ahe. Tauren hunters revere the king of the savannah cats as mercy and death. His swift strike leaves his quarry no time for terror or suffering. The horn belongs at his lair, among the giant kodo bones behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads.

faq.q: What does the Horn of Echeyakee do?
aliases: what is horn of echeyakee for
faq.answer: The horn calls Echeyakee, the elusive white savannah cat. Sound it near the giant kodo bones northeast of the Crossroads, and the beast appears for a hunter to face.

faq.q: Where does the horn come from?
faq.answer: At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Sergra Darkthorn, an orc huntress, gives the horn to those seeking to prove their subtlety and tracking skill.

faq.q: What does the name Echeyakee mean?
faq.answer: In Taur-ahe, the Tauren tongue, Echeyakee means “Whitemist.” The name honors his pale coat and silent passage through dry grasses.

faq.q: Where do you blow the horn?
faq.answer: Sound the horn among the giant kodo ribs and skeletal remains behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads, where the white lion roams.

angles.text: As a hunter, you face Echeyakee in a legendary rite of passage. Your senses are tested against a predator renowned across the Barrens for near-flawless stealth.
As a tauren, you know Echeyakee’s hunt carries spiritual weight. Your people see his swift, painless kill as both mercy and the harsh necessity of death.
